@okiela_io The free shipping bar. Discount the SKU, the cart drops under the threshold, shipping reappears. And whether Shopify prices that rate before or after the code, I've never found documented. So I run the cart instead of assuming. It decides whether the deal costs them mo

@okiela_io Depends how the % was built. As a product discount it won't stack with a Buy X get Y on non-Plus plans: the customer gets whichever is worth more, not both. The bar promised both. As an order discount they combine. Run the $52 cart with the gift and see if the % surviv

@okiela_io Shopify reports will not give you that band. I export orders to a sheet and bucket the totals around the threshold.
And the test for a gap product is narrow: its margin has to cover the label it unlocks. Below that, every unlock is a paid loss dressed as growth.

@paulinaashleigh Before adding traffic, check what a visit is worth today. Last 30 days: revenue divided by sessions.
If that number is low, more visitors mostly adds cost. The same effort spent on what one visit brings in pays on every session you already have.

@okiela_io One number tells you whether the bar is honest: the share of orders landing within five percent above the threshold.
Full band, the bar works. Empty band with a crowd sitting just under it, and you are training people toward a number that never pays off.

@okiela_io The threshold is only half of it. It works when you actually sell something in the gap.
Most stores set 50 with nothing between 30 and 47 except a 3-pack nobody wants. Fix the catalogue in that band before touching the bar.

@okiela_io The rule wins at checkout, but the bar is what shapes the cart.
It shows up as carts clustering right at the old number, then dropping at the shipping step. The cluster is the tell, not the abandon rate.

@uziprints Yes, the one on the page right after payment. One tap, no card re-entered.
Catch: it only renders for direct card orders via Shopify Payments. Shop Pay and the wallets never see it. So judge it on eligible orders, not total.

@h4harisali Fair — though eligibility isn't a product question, it's a payment-method one. Same store, same offer, different denominator depending on how people checked out. Have you ever counted it on a client? Genuinely curious what it lands at.

@h4harisali Under 16-30% there's a second number: what share of orders even reach that page. Subscription orders and some express checkouts never see it. Do you measure take rate on total orders, or on eligible ones? Those two can be far apart.

@alexpagepilot The bar works. The threshold is where it goes wrong. Set it below your AOV and you're paying shipping on orders that were already converting - the lift shows in the dashboard, the margin doesn't. Better to set it against the spread of your order values than a round

@ecomchasedimond Three of these five buy AOV with margin. The one that doesn't is the post-purchase offer: it fires after payment is captured, so it can't cost you conversion the way anything added before checkout can.
@kurtinc Did any of those 10 stores run post-purchase surveys? Attributed vs self-reported usually splits hard on exactly this. The no-click paths don't leave a referrer to measure.
